title: Identification of objective markers for the evaluation and prediction of the treatment of children and adolescents with ADHD
summary: The aim of this study is to investigate objectively occurring changes during the treatment of children and adolescents with AD(H)D. The treatment of AD(H)D includes comprehensive advice and may include pharmacotherapy. Currently the effects of medical treatment are evaluated in a rather subjective way such as observations made by parents, teachers or medical professionals. The identification of objective markers is necessary to determine treatment effects with greater certainty. To investigate which potential markers are suitable, children and adolescents (8-16 years) with confirmed diagnosis of AD(H)D prior to planned medication are included in this study. Clinical symptoms will be assessed with questionnaires, neuropsychological and language based assessments. Moreover,  smartphone-based movement and activity data will be collected to assess hyperactivity. To assess brain imaging based correlates, a subgroup of the included children/adolescents shall be examined with Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI). All assessments will be prior to treatment onset and eight weeks are treatment initiation.
conditions: Other specified behavioural and emotional disorders with onset usually occurring in childhood and adolescence

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Children/adolescents with AD(H)D:
1. AD(H)D diagnosis according to ICD10/DMS-5 
2. Children/adolescents aged 8 to 16
3. Written consent
4. Consent of parents/legal guardians
5. Persons who are legally competent and mentally able to follow the instructions of the staff

Healthy controls:
1. Children/adolescents aged 8 to 16
2. Written consent
3. Consent of parents/legal guardians
4. Persons who are legally competent and mentally able to follow the instructions of the staff
Exclusion criteria:
Children/adolescents with AD(H)D:
1. IQ < 80
2. Diagnosed autism spectrum disorder, epilepsy or brain-organic damage 
3. Persons who are placed in an institution by order of the authorities or the court
4. Persons who are in a dependent or employment relationship with the researcher

Healthy controls:
1. IQ < 80
2. Diagnosed AD(H)D, autism spectrum disorder, epilepsy or brain-organic damage 
3. Persons who are placed in an institution by order of the authorities or the court
4. Persons who are in a dependent or employment relationship with the researcher
